🇲🇽⚡ <u>MEXICO'S AI BOOM HITS THE GRID</u>

Mexico's data-center capacity nearly tripled in two years — from 115 MW in early 2024 to 279 MW today, 72% of it in Querétaro, with the industry targeting 1.5 GW by 2030. The catch isn't demand, it's the grid: under the old neoliberal model only 11% of the approved transmission budget was ever spent, per IMCO — which makes CFE's expansion the real nearshoring battleground. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>76 BILLION PESOS FOR MEXICO'S FORGOTTEN EAST</u>

The Plan Integral for the eastern State of Mexico just hit 40% completion: 121 projects worth 75.8 billion pesos in water, health, housing and transit for the 10 million people of Neza, Chalco, Ecatepec, Chimalhuacán and Valle de Chalco — the densest, most neglected corner of the country. This month IMSS breaks ground on four new childcare centers, and Governor Delfina Gómez reports homicides in the zone already down 33%.

🇲🇽💧 <u>MEXICO RECLAIMS 5 BILLION m³ OF WATER FROM PRIVATE HANDS</u>

After December's reform stripped water of its status as a tradable commodity and restored it as a human right, Mexico has recovered more than 5 billion cubic meters from private concessions — enough to supply 90 million people for a year. Cities like Mexicali and Tijuana now hold their water rights directly, instead of buying back what neoliberalism privatized out from under them.

🇲🇽📉 <u>HOMICIDES DOWN 51% IN UNDER TWO YEARS</u>

Mexico's daily homicide rate has fallen 51% since Sheinbaum took office — from 86.9 killings a day in September 2024 to 42.5 in July 2026, 44 fewer bodies every single day, per the national security secretariat (SESNSP). July marked the lowest monthly average in 11 years.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRICIEST ELECTIONS IN MEXICAN HISTORY</u>

Mexico's 2027 midterms are shaping up as the costliest ever: the INE and eight parties are asking for 51 billion pesos — a 45.6% jump over 2024 — just to fill 21,000 seats. President Sheinbaum notes that's roughly what Mexico still pays every two years in interest on the 1990s bank bailout the same establishment left behind.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>OLMECA REFINERY HITS RECORD OUTPUT</u>

The Dos Bocas refinery the neoliberals swore would never work just posted its best month ever — 252,000 barrels a day in July, up 79% from June — refining 27% of all the fuel Mexico makes, now the single most productive plant in the country.

🇲🇽🚆 "In about three years, you'll be able to go from here all the way to Mexico City by train." Saltillo sits on the Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo and central corridors of Mexico's rail revival — 2,377 km of new passenger and freight track, double what the entire previous administration built. Passenger service starts returning between late 2026 and 2027. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽✊ 884,942 people in Coahuila now receive a Bienestar payment — 19,223 million pesos delivered. "We defend love made policy, through the Programas de Bienestar," Sheinbaum said in Saltillo. Pensions for seniors and for women 60–64, student scholarships and disability support are now written into Mexico's Constitution as rights — not charity that can be taken away. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽✊ "There is no divorce, no distance. We are one and the same — government and people of Mexico." At her "Honestidad y Resultados" event in Saltillo, Coahuila, Sheinbaum described the Fourth Transformation as a government fused with its people, not standing above them. Coahuila drew one of the largest crowds of her national accountability tour. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Saltillo, Coahuila

🇲🇽🌎 "September is the month of the homeland — remember the origin of our country: sovereign, independent, free." Speaking in Coahuila, Sheinbaum tied her government's project to Mexico's founding: a country born sovereign and independent. In 11 days the nation marks the Grito de Independencia — Hidalgo's 1810 call in Dolores for the people to fight for freedom. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Coahuila
